channel.title: Pier & Point · Pier 70
channel.description: What happened or was announced on the ground at Pier 70, San Francisco: dated milestones and the changes they brought to the record. Every item names its source.

item.title: Added · Piers 68 & 70 Dry Docks: On July 15, 2026, Potrero View reported that the Port expects…
item.description: On July 15, 2026, Potrero View reported that the Port expects initial plans to be completed by next March, with a contract for demolition work tendered the second half of 2027 (the reporter's wording, not a quotation). Source: https://www.potreroview.net/large-ship-repair-fades-into-san-francisco-history/.

item.title: Expected · 22nd St Caltrain Station ADA Access Improvement: Expected, not scheduled: the… (~2029)
item.description: Expected, not scheduled: the project is expected to open for use in 2029, subject to funding. The month differs by source: June 2029 (SFCTA's April 28, 2026 post, "seeking construction funding to implement the project by June 2029", and the April 14 presentation, "Open for use expected June 2029"), December 2029 (SFCTA's April 14 packet, project description: "have the project open for use by December 2029, subject to funding availability"; its allocation form lists "Open for Use" in April-June 2029) and "project completion by the end of 2029" (The Voice of San Francisco, October 6, 2026). Construction was not yet funded in April 2026; the FTA announced a $14.1 million award in September 2026, but no source gives a construction schedule. (~2029). Source: San Francisco County Transportation Authority, 2026-04-28; San Francisco County Transportation Authority, 2026-04-14; The Voice of San Francisco, 2026-10-06.
item.source: San Francisco County Transportation Authority, 2026-04-28; San Francisco County Transportation Authority, 2026-04-14; The Voice of San Francisco, 2026-10-06

item.title: Added · Pier 70 Parcel E3: RASA World's one-day festival Pier Play San Francisco, headlined by…
item.description: RASA World's one-day festival Pier Play San Francisco, headlined by BLOND:ISH, was held on Sep 19, 2026 on Pier 70's Parcel E3. Elevation Sky Park's own page (checked Sep 29, 2026) calls the site 'the future home of Elevation Sky Park', invites sign-ups for opening announcements and gives no opening date; the July 2026 release had said the campus would open in phases beginning September 2026. No source shows the venue itself open. Source: https://elevationskypark.com/.

item.title: Milestone · 22nd St Caltrain Station ADA Access Improvement: The Federal Transit… (~Sep 2026)
item.description: The Federal Transit Administration announces an All Stations Accessibility Program award of $14.1 million to the Peninsula Corridor Joint Powers Board for ADA improvements at the 22nd Street station (an announced date, not a grant agreement or construction start): Trains.com, published September 16, 2026, says the agency announced the awards "last week". Railway Supply (September 12, 2026) says the FTA published its selection list on September 10 and Progressive Railroading is dated September 11; the FTA's own announcement was not read. The amount is close to the funding gap SFCTA's April 2026 plan had left as "Planned TBD". (~Sep 2026). Source: Trains.com, 2026-09-16; Railway Supply, 2026-09-12; Progressive Railroading, 2026-09-11.

item.title: Expected · Pier 70 Parcel C1: Port Commission: Port staff and the… (late 2026 or early 2027)
item.description: Port Commission: Port staff and the developer are drafting amendments to the DDA and related transaction documents "for consideration by the Port Commission and Board of Supervisors by the end of this year or early next year" (Item 11A, memo of Aug 7, 2026, p.2 and p.6). Port Commission minutes of Aug 11, 2026 (p.7): staff and Brookfield "expect to return with proposed amendments in late 2026 or early 2027". The source gives no hearing date. The date shown is the early end of that window (December 2026); "early next year" falls in 2027. The same report proposes extending the term of the DDA, Development Agreement and Master Lease by 5 years. (late 2026 or early 2027). Source: Port of San Francisco, 2026-08-07; Port of San Francisco, 2026-08-11.
item.source: Port of San Francisco, 2026-08-07; Port of San Francisco, 2026-08-11

item.title: Milestone · 22nd St Caltrain Station ADA Access Improvement: SFCTA's Transportation… (Apr 14, 2026)
item.description: SFCTA's Transportation Authority Board packet for its April 14, 2026 meeting recommends $1,300,000 in Prop L funds for the project's design phase, part of a total funding plan of $19,134,000 (Planning/Conceptual Engineering $734,000 already spent via Prop K; Design Engineering $1,300,000 via Prop L; Construction $17,100,000, an engineer's estimate at 30% design). item.title: Milestone · Piers 68 & 70 Dry Docks: Capital Planning Committee item: the Port asks… (Feb 9, 2026)
item.description: Capital Planning Committee item: the Port asks the committee to consider and approve a $18.5M supplemental appropriation, in a memo dated 2026-02-09 whose cost table shows $61.2M total estimated cost to stabilize and dispose of Dry Dock No. 2 and the Eureka Dry Dock. About $20.0M of that is the $18.5M requested appropriation plus $1.5M of existing BAE settlement funds; the other $41.2M is an anticipated FY2026-27 appropriation ("anticipated additional appropriation of funds in the FY 2026-27 capital budget"). No source read reports the committee's decision or whether either appropriation was adopted. (Feb 9, 2026). Source: Port of San Francisco (memo from the Acting Executive Director to the Capital Planning Committee, hosted on the City's onesanfrancisco.org), 2026-02-09; City and County of San Francisco Capital Planning Committee, 2026-02-09.

item.title: Expected · Piers 68 & 70 Dry Docks: Expected, as announced by the Port in January… (~Sep 2026)
item.description: Expected, as announced by the Port in January 2026, and since superseded: Port staff anticipate advertising a contract for demolition services in the summer of 2026 (memo dated 2026-01-09: "Port staff anticipates advertising a contract for demolition services in the summer of 2026"). The Port's Feb 9, 2026 presentation to the Capital Planning Committee instead lists "Spring 2026: Award of final demolition and construction contract". An expected date; no source read reports that either happened, and the later reports (see the 2026-07 entry) put the tender in the second half of 2027. Dated to the end of summer 2026. (~Sep 2026). Source: Port of San Francisco / Port Commission, 2026-01-09; City and County of San Francisco Capital Planning Committee, 2026-02-09.
